gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
We'd better not ___ the neighbours again.
gaps.explanation: had better + bare infinitive (not comes after better): better not disturb.
Negative infinitive: promised not to be late — 'not' goes before 'to'.

gaps.sentence: We're looking forward to ___ from you soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Look forward to + -ing' — 'to' is a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: Do you fancy ___ to the cinema tonight?
gaps.explanation: fancy + -ing (informal British): Do you fancy going…?

gaps.sentence: I was made ___ the dustbin lorry at six in the morning.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, make takes the to-infinitive: was made to wait.

gaps.sentence: The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)

gaps.sentence: He apologized for ___ so abrupt in the meeting.
